text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- First meeting of Algeria's first pluralist parliament opens a Second Republic era and buries the sole party ruling regime.

- "Terrorists" break into home in Bouzareah district, on northern edge of Algiers, and cut the throats of five family members. The family children escaped to alert neighbours who arrived late. Gunmen blow up home at El Biar district destroying half the house but causing no casualties. Four people, including three construction workers, were killed on Chenoua seafront in Tipaza province, west of Algiers.

- Political parties represented in newly-elected National Assembly (lower house) resume talks to try to build consensus on the name of the house speaker. The house resumes its session on Tuesday after its maiden meeting on Sunday.
- The elected house holds first meeting: the train of democracy pulls out of station.
- Prime Minister Ahmed Ouyahia, who was reappointed on Saturday by President Liamine Zeroual, has to clear more hurdles to form his cabinet as local elections are likely to be held in September.
